newsitem.title: UK: Mideast/east clean tanker rates fall in slow market.
newsitem.headline: Mideast/east clean tanker rates fall in slow market.

text.p: Clean tanker rates were steady to softer this week with trade slack on Middle East/east routes, while in the west levels managed to hold up reasonably well and in the Mediterranean they actually rose, brokers said on Friday.

Brokers E.A. Gibson said in their weekly tanker report that "the combination of poor demand and low rate levels in the Middle East is particularly worrying for owners who must be hoping that it does not herald a general depreciation in rates over the spring period."
They said Middle East/India 40,000/45,000 tonne cargoes had fallen below W180, with 30,000 tonnes little better at below W200.
But they said the Med market was "now showing signs of real recovery" after a very slow start to the week, with 27,250 tonne naphtha cargoes firming to W205 and 30,000 tonnes of gas oil at W180/190.
Brokers also noted good Asian demand from the Med/Black Sea and the Baltic, with 60,000 tonnes said done from Ventspils to Singapore at $1.8 million for Cargill.
The inter-U.K./Cont market was very quiet with only a couple of fixtures reported, while the Caribbean sector was no livelier with 30,000 tonnes upcoast around W260.
